claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

eu_status.description: The claimant's EU Settlement Scheme status, where relevant.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm responsible for one child. My son Alex is 11 years old and lives with me here at home. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me ask you a few more questions to determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation:

**Are you the person who is primarily responsible for Alex's day-to-day care? In other words, do you provide for his needs such as food, clothes, and other essentials?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm the one who takes care of Alex day-to-day - I provide everything he needs like food, clothes, and all his essentials.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just a few more questions:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Let me ask about Alex's current situation:

**Is Alex currently in full-time education at school?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's in school full-time. He's 11, so he's in Year 7.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex living with you at home full-time, or does he spend time living elsewhere (for example, in hospital, care, or with someone else)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with me at home full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

**Do you or your partner (if you have one) have an individual income over £60,000 per year?** 

(This won't affect your eligibility to receive Child Benefit, but it may mean you need to pay a tax charge called the High Income Child Benefit Charge.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not get into those details right now - I'm mainly just trying to find out if I'm eligible to claim it in the first place.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's absolutely fine - you don't need to share that information for me to assess your basic eligibility.

Based on what you've told me, I now have enough information to make an assessment. Let me review your situation for Alex:

- Alex is 11 years old (under 16)
- He lives with you full-time in the UK
- You are responsible for his day-to-day care and provide for his needs
- He is in full-time education at school
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him

You meet all the key eligibility criteria for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

You meet all the necessary requirements:
- You're responsible for a child under 16
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with you full-time
- You provide for his day-to-day needs
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit. If you need information on how to claim, you can contact HMRC or visit the government website to start your application.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
